scope: NY-7.RP.1, NY-7.RP.3, NY-7.EE.1, NY-7.EE.2 on the grade 7 test

g7-2023-033.quote: Lin ran 2 3/4 miles in 2/5 of an hour.
g7-2023-033.why: Item asks for average speed in miles per hour from 6 1/2 miles in 2/3 hour. The activity gives exactly that structure - mixed-number miles over a fractional hour - and asks students to compare the resulting speeds.

g7-2024-043.quote: Lin ran 2 3/4 miles in 2/5 of an hour.
g7-2024-043.why: Item asks miles per hour from 5 1/2 miles in 2 1/5 hours. The activity has students divide a mixed number of miles by a fractional number of hours to get each runner's speed.

g7-2026-044.quote: Lin ran 2 3/4 miles in 2/5 of an hour.
g7-2026-044.why: Item gives two cyclists' fractional distances and times and asks for the difference in their average speeds; this activity asks for two runners' speeds from fractional distances and times so they can be compared.

g7-2025-044.quote: divide a fraction by a fraction to calculate the unit rate
g7-2025-044.why: Item asks gallons per hour from 3/8 gallon per 1 1/2 hours. The activity is the place the curriculum asks students to divide a fraction by a fraction to get a unit rate.

g7-2025-027.quote: divide a fraction by a fraction to calculate the unit rate
g7-2025-027.why: Item asks miles per gallon from 30 miles and 1 2/3 gallons - a whole number divided by a mixed number. The activity is where dividing by a fractional amount to find a unit rate is taught; the item's dividend happens to be whole.

g7-2024-026.quote: divide a fraction by a fraction to calculate the unit rate
g7-2024-026.why: Item asks cups per batch from 2 5/8 cups over 3 1/2 batches. Same computation the activity asks for - a unit rate found by dividing a fraction by a fraction - in a recipe rather than a speed context.

g7-2026-005.quote: divide a fraction by a fraction to calculate the unit rate
g7-2026-005.why: Item asks gallons per hour from 3,000 gallons in 2 1/2 hours. The activity is where students divide by a fractional amount of time to find a constant-rate unit rate.

g7-2023-023.quote: a 32% increase followed by a 10% decrease of that new amount
g7-2023-023.why: Item applies a 10% increase to week 1 and then a 15% increase to week 2, so the second percentage acts on the new amount. This activity is built on exactly that point - a markup followed by a discount off the new retail price, which is why it does not add to a single percentage.

g7-2023-032.quote: The tax rate at this restaurant is 9.5%. Another person’s subtotal is $24.95.
g7-2023-032.why: Item takes a $58.20 restaurant subtotal and adds 5% sales tax and a 20% tip. This is the one activity that works a restaurant subtotal, its sales tax, and its tip together, and its second question computes the tax from a rate and a subtotal.

g7-2023-038.quote: After the discount, how much will a customer pay for this vehicle?
g7-2023-038.why: Item asks the total a customer pays for two services after an 18% discount on their combined price. The activity asks the same question - the price a customer pays after a percent discount is taken off a retail price.

g7-2023-048.activity: More Shampoo and a Discounted Shirt
g7-2023-048.quote: a percent increase or percent decrease and the original amount
g7-2023-048.why: Item gives two original ticket prices and two reductions (25% off, 1/3 off) and asks for each reduced price so they can be compared. This activity is where students are given the original amount and a percent decrease and must produce the new amount; no activity compares two competing discounts.

g7-2024-029.quote: By how much will they mark up the price of the vehicle?
g7-2024-029.why: Item asks for 35% of the money 500 gift cards at $15.00 bring in. Lesson 11 is where a business's cut of a sale price is computed (this activity asks for the dollar amount of a 32% markup on $12,000, and the lesson's practice problems ask what commission a salesperson earns on a $495 couch).

g7-2024-034.quote: It costs $3.45 to buy 3/4 foot of electrical wire.
g7-2024-034.why: Item gives $23.75 for 2 1/2 hours and asks the pay for 5 3/4 hours. This Cool-down gives a price for a fractional amount and asks the price for a different fractional amount - the same proportional scaling with fractions, taught in this lesson's abbreviated-table activities.

g7-2024-041.quote: The original price of a bicycle was $375. Now it is on sale for $295.
g7-2024-041.why: Item gives a $55.00 original price and a $38.50 price paid and asks for the percent discount. The activity's third problem is the same question in the same context - original price, sale price, what percentage was the markdown.

g7-2024-048.quote: After a 25% discount, the price of a T-shirt was $12.
g7-2024-048.why: The item's hard step is working backward from a $460 discounted price and a 20% discount to the $575 original; this activity's fifth problem asks exactly that. The item then adds 8% tax to both prices and differences them, which is Lesson 10 and Lesson 12 work, so no single activity asks the whole question.

g7-2025-048.quote: the total savings after various discounts are applied to different items
g7-2025-048.why: Item applies a 10% discount to one shirt and a 25% discount to another and asks the total spent. This activity is the curriculum's multi-item, multi-discount totaling task; the plain single-discount computation itself is Lesson 6.

g7-2026-012.quote: A salesperson sold a car for $18,250, and their commission is $693.50.
g7-2026-012.why: Item gives $1,200 principal, 4 years, $144 simple interest and asks the annual rate, which reduces to: $36 is what percentage of $1,200. This activity asks that shape of question from dollar amounts, but nothing in Grade 7 develops simple interest over several years - interest appears only as a card-sort category and as one-year practice problems.

g7-2026-017.quote: They are on sale for 20% off. A sales tax of 6%
g7-2026-017.why: Item takes a $279.00 laptop, applies a 10% coupon, then an 8.875% tax on the discounted price. This Cool-down is the same problem with different numbers - normal price, percent off, then sales tax added to the sale price.

g7-2023-041.quote: an expression that is equivalent to 1/2 (8y − x − 12)
g7-2023-041.why: Item asks students to write 1/2(18y - 2y + 10) as the sum of two unlike terms. This activity asks for an equivalent expression for one-half of a three-term expression with subtraction, using the distributive property with boxes to organize the work; combining 18y and -2y is Lesson 20's skill.

g7-2024-013.why: Item expands 3.6(x - 5) + 2.5(x + 4) and collects like terms. This activity is where two parenthesized linear expressions are joined and matched to forms with fewer terms; non-unit decimal coefficients appear only in this lesson's practice problems.

g7-2024-037.quote: Write each expression with fewer terms.
g7-2024-037.why: Item asks for an expression equivalent to 17 1/3 x - 7/2 x, a single subtraction of like terms. This Cool-down asks exactly that (10x - 2x); the fractional coefficients are Unit 5 arithmetic and appear in no activity of this lesson.

g7-2024-046.activity: Factoring and Expanding With Negative Numbers
g7-2024-046.quote: Each expression involves subtraction or negative numbers
g7-2024-046.why: Item asks students to expand -8(4 - x) + 20 and show the properties used. This activity's table opens with the worked example -3(5 - 2y) = -15 + 6y, the same negative-coefficient expansion the item requires.

g7-2025-020.quote: Some students are trying to write an expression with fewer terms
g7-2025-020.why: Item asks for an expression equivalent to 4(3x - 1.25) - 2(3.5x + 2), where the trap is distributing the -2 over both terms. This activity has students find and describe exactly that sign error while writing an expression with fewer terms.

g7-2025-046.quote: write an expression with fewer terms that is equivalent to
g7-2025-046.why: Item asks students to simplify -5y + 3 - 6y + 10y - 1 completely. This activity asks for an expression with fewer terms equivalent to 6j + 4d - 2j + 3d - the same collecting of like terms across a subtraction.

g7-2026-011.quote: Some students are trying to write an expression with fewer terms
g7-2026-011.why: Item asks for an expression equivalent to 3(5x + 2) - 2(6x - 7), so the -2 must reach the -7. This activity is where students diagnose that exact mishandling of a subtracted product while writing fewer terms.

g7-2026-023.quote: Some students are trying to write an expression with fewer terms
g7-2026-023.why: Item asks for an expression equivalent to 7 - 2(3x + 6) - 4x. The activity's expression is the same shape - a constant minus a coefficient times a binomial - and the two wrong student methods it shows produce the item's distractors.

g7-2026-032.quote: Expand to write an equivalent expression: - 1/2 (-2x + 4y)
g7-2026-032.why: Item asks for an expression equivalent to -1/4(12x - 6). This Cool-down asks students to expand -1/2(-2x + 4y): the same distribution of a negative fractional coefficient over a binomial.

g7-2026-041.quote: Some students are trying to write an expression with fewer terms
g7-2026-041.why: Item asks students to simplify -3/4(4x - 8) + (x - 2): expand a negative fractional coefficient, then collect like terms. This activity asks for an expression with fewer terms from an expression containing a product to expand; the fractional-coefficient version of it is a practice problem in this lesson, not an activity.

g7-2023-021.activity: Factoring and Expanding With Negative Numbers
g7-2023-021.quote: In each row, write the equivalent expression.
g7-2023-021.why: Item asks which expression is equivalent to 8b + 8g in a total-price context; the answer is 8(b + g). This activity's table asks students to move between expanded and factored forms, including pulling a common numeric factor out of two different variable terms (6a - 2b, 20x - 10y + 15z).

g7-2024-011.lessonTitle: Solving Problems About Percent Increase or Decrease
g7-2024-011.quote: An item costs x dollars and then a 20% discount is applied.
g7-2024-011.why: Item asks which pair of expressions both give a shirt's price after a 15% discount (n - 0.15n and 0.85n). This Warm-up asks students to select all expressions representing the price after a 20% discount, and its list contains both x - 20/100x and 0.80x.

g7-2025-021.lessonTitle: Solving Problems About Percent Increase or Decrease
g7-2025-021.quote: An item costs x dollars and then a 20% discount is applied.
g7-2025-021.why: Item asks which expression, besides t - 0.10t, gives a sweater's sale price (0.90t). This Warm-up is the same question at 20%: select every expression that represents the price after the discount.

g7-2025-036.lessonTitle: Solving Problems About Percent Increase or Decrease
g7-2025-036.quote: An item costs x dollars and then a 20% discount is applied.
g7-2025-036.why: Item asks which expression represents a phone's value after a 20% decrease (0.8x). This Warm-up asks for the expressions representing an item's price after a 20% discount, and 0.80x is one of the choices.

g7-2026-036.lessonTitle: Solving Problems About Percent Increase or Decrease
g7-2026-036.quote: An item costs x dollars and then a 20% discount is applied.
g7-2026-036.why: Item asks which expression, besides x - 0.25x, gives the final price after 25% off (0.75x). This Warm-up asks students to select all expressions for the price after a percent discount, listing both the subtraction form and the single-factor form.
